Package index

Fitting

The estimator. rails() calibrates the whole cohort; rails_subgroup() runs the same procedure independently within each stratum.

rails()
RAILS: raking with assisted nested propensity score and LIFO selection
rails_subgroup()
Subgroup RAILS

Inspecting a fit

S3 methods on rails_fit, plus a diagnostic that works on any weight vector.

weights(<rails_fit>) weights(<rails_subgroup_fit>)
Extract RAILS weights
summary(<rails_fit>) print(<summary.rails_fit>)
Summarize a RAILS fit
plot(<rails_fit>)
Plot the RAILS weight distribution
weight_summary()
Weight diagnostics

Inference

rails_var() is the reference for inference on a weighted mean. rails_design() hands the weights to the survey package for everything else.

rails_var()
Variance of a RAILS-weighted mean
rails_design()
Hand RAILS weights to the survey package

Preparing inputs

Cell tables and population margins, from your own data or from ACS PUMS.

rails_cells()
Aggregate microdata into covariate cells
rails_totals()
Population margins matching a cell table
pums_fetch()
Download ACS PUMS microdata from the Census API
pums_recode()
Recode raw ACS PUMS into RAILS analysis variables
pums_reference()
Build a RAILS reference sample from recoded PUMS
pums_variables()
ACS PUMS variables RAILS uses

Simulation

A synthetic population with a known truth, used by every example and vignette here.

rails_simulate()
Simulate a population with a biased volunteer sample

Algorithm stages

Exported so the individual steps can be inspected or reused. rails() calls them for you.

nps_weights()
Nested propensity score weights
gvs_step()
Greedy variable selection: test one candidate interaction
